messages:
sam-remote: Hey @people-ops — quick q: planning a 4-week trip to Singapore next month, will be working remote the whole time. Do WFH stipend and benefits continue? Any payroll / tax steps I need to take? Also worried about creating a tax nexus for Redwood if I'm in-country 4 weeks.

maria-peopleops: Congrats! Short answer: maybe. Company policy allows temporary remote work abroad up to 30 days with manager sign-off and prior notice. 4 weeks = 28 days so fits, but you still must fill the Remote Work Abroad form and get manager + People Ops sign-off.

jenna-peopleops: Stipend: monthly WFH allowance is normally pro-rated if you change home base mid-month. If you're just traveling and your legal work address stays the same, stipend generally continues unchanged for short trips. We'll confirm payroll logic for your payroll cycle.

liam-finance: From finance side: 28 days typically won't create corporate tax residency (183-day rule) but SG has its own regs around presence and employment. For that duration we usually don't see employer tax nexus, but we'll run a quick check with our international tax advisor. If you end up extending beyond 30 days we need payroll review and possibly local registration.

maria-peopleops: Action items for you: 1) Fill form: https://redwood.internal/remote-abroad (select "Singapore", travel dates). 2) Confirm manager approval in thread (please @ your manager). 3) Upload passport copy + return flight ETA if asked. 4) If any client meetings or paid local work, tell us — that changes the equation.

sam-remote: Thanks — my manager @alex-eng is looped in. No client meetings planned. I'll submit the form today. On stipend: I get paid monthly on the 1st — will proration hit me if I leave mid-cycle?

jenna-peopleops: If your travel starts in the middle of a stipend period we typically prorate that month's allowance. Example: monthly stipend $200, you are away 10 days of 30 -> $133. We'll calculate exact days and you'll see line item on next payroll.

liam-finance: Also flag for payroll: if you receive any foreign-source income while there (e.g., per diem from a local partner), that could create additional reporting. If you want, we'll put a temporary flag on your payroll record so we can re-run calculations before the trip.

payroll-bot: Reminder: Please submit Remote Work Abroad form at least 5 business days before start date to avoid payroll hold. :bell: 

sam-remote: Got it, thanks all. Submitting now. cc @maria-peopleops for final sign-off. :thumbsup: 

maria-peopleops: Received — I'll review once form submitted and confirm within 48 hours. If tax advisor flags anything unexpected we'll reach out before your trip.
